The main analysis is hierarchical (section 3, subsections 3.1–3.3, and two 3.2.x subsubsections), but the conclusion returns to level-one numbering.
Data availability and funding statements appear after the conclusion and before references.
The article’s structure belongs to a legal normative-research paper; it should not be generalized to experimental/scientific papers or student reports.
visual_features: No rendered PDF inspection was done. The text layer includes a journal/issue/page running line and DOI metadata, but this alone does not establish visual typography, margins, colors, figure legibility, or page layout.
privacy_and_quality_cautions: The published article discusses public court decisions and names individuals in its body; no such case narrative or individual names are copied into this structure record.
The author contact email visible in the PDF is intentionally not retained.
License, bibliographic identity and public access were verified; legal assertions and court-decision details have not been independently re-audited.

review_flags.benchmark_role: open-license legal research article structure exemplar; not a gold standard for legal accuracy or prose
review_flags.generalization_status: single item from one journal; contributes to cross-journal variation but no universal academic-paper inference
